AcceptanceBand.description:
How far predicted and measured may differ and still be called agreement.

``fraction`` is the half-width as a fraction of the prediction: 0.05 is ±5%. ``source``
is required and may not be blank, because a corridor nobody can attribute is the
arbitrary one ASME V&V 10's teaching material warns against — the reader has to be able
to disagree with the band rather than with the verdict it produced.
AcceptanceBand.title: AcceptanceBand

AppliedFactor.description:
A factor a check applied inside its capacity, where its verdict cannot show it.

A check judged at a required safety factor of 1.0 has put its whole margin inside the
capacity: a pile's allowable load is its ultimate capacity over a factor of safety, and a
BTH-1 allowable is a strength over the design factor N_d. The verdict then reads "1.0
required", and the conservatism the reader is relying on is nowhere on the card. The
check records it here, so the margin ledger can itemize it like any other.

``authority`` is the clause that obliges the factor. ``None`` means an election or a
default nobody cited, and the ledger files it as such rather than as a code's.
AppliedFactor.title: AppliedFactor

CheckStatus.description:
A check's outcome.

``NOT_EVALUATED`` is never silently treated as a pass — a check that could
not run is reported as such. ``OVER_MARGIN`` is a passing check whose margin
ran past a declared upper band: acceptable, never blocking, but flagged so an
over-engineered candidate is as visible as a failing one.

``OUT_OF_DEPTH`` is a check the document *deliberately deferred*: the spec declared a
screening depth this check sits below. It is not blocking — the engineer asked for a
concept screen and got one — and it is not ``NOT_EVALUATED`` either, because "I chose
not to screen that yet" and "I could not screen that" are different facts about a
design that a reader acts on differently. Every surface states both counts.

``WARNING`` is a check that met its hard limit and entered a caution band its document
declared: material inside a keepout's clearance margin that does not reach the protected
core. It is not a pass, so a card holding one does not pass, and it is not a failure,
so it neither blocks as one nor reads as one.
CheckStatus.title: CheckStatus

Comparison.description:
What a check measured, what it was judged against, and which way passes.

A check that compares two quantities used to state the comparison as a *sentence*,
written at screening time. A screen does not know what unit system its result will be
read in, so a US-customary report printed a deflection verdict in millimetres directly
beneath a worked derivation in inches — same check, same page, two systems.

The numbers travel instead, and the sentence is rendered by whoever is showing it. That
is the shape :meth:`ScorecardEntry.from_safety_factor` has always had: it writes its
line from the two factors rather than taking one from its caller, which is why the
safety-factor half of the library never had this defect.

``minimum_decimals`` is the precision floor the sentence starts from; it widens from
there until the two figures are distinguishable, because a FAIL reading "15.000 mm vs
limit 15.000 mm" states the opposite of its own verdict.
Comparison.title: Comparison

Correlation.description:
One prediction compared with one measurement of the same quantity.

``predicted`` is what the driving check computed; ``measured`` is what the recorded
verification outcome measured. They are converted into the prediction's own unit before
anything is compared, so a preload predicted in kN and measured in lbf correlates.

The test record travels with the comparison — the date, the performer and the
instrument — because the escaped-defect process downstream needs the record, not a
reference to one, and because a correlation whose instrument nobody can name is a claim.

:attr:`verdict` is ``NOT_EVALUATED`` with no band: both values and the ratio are still
reported, and :meth:`__str__` names the band it needs.

citation.default: ASME V&V 10 vocabulary (verification, validation, validation domain)
citation.title: Citation

difference.description: Measured minus predicted, in the prediction's own unit.

ratio.description: Measured over predicted, both in the prediction's unit. 1.0 is exact agreement.
ratio.title: Ratio

verdict.description: Agreement, or which way it fell outside the declared band.

Correlation.title: Correlation

CorrelationVerdict.description: What the comparison said. Never what the check said.
CorrelationVerdict.title: CorrelationVerdict

Derivation.description:
A check's worked calculation: formula, substitution, result, citation.

``symbolic`` is the governing formula written the way the source writes it
(``"σ_b = M · c / I"``); ``inputs`` supply every symbol on its right-hand side;
``result`` is the left-hand side with the computed value; and ``citation`` names
the handbook section or standard clause the formula comes from. Every symbol
used carries its own glossary line, so the derivation is readable without the
source book open.
Derivation.title: Derivation

DerivationAbsence.description:
Why a check renders no worked calculation — the two kinds that are finished.

Neither is a shortfall. A ``LOOKUP`` has no arithmetic between its two numbers:
an exemption, an identification line, a table comparison, a consistency verdict.
A ``NUMERIC_RESULT`` has real mathematics behind it and no substitutable line —
its value is the root of an equation, solved rather than evaluated, so the
inputs/outputs table is the correct rendering for it rather than a shortfall.

The third kind a check can be in — **debt**, a closed form nobody has written
down yet — is deliberately not a member. Debt is the *absence* of a declaration,
recorded per clause in ``docs/api/underived-checks.txt`` where the ratchet keeps
the list downward-only. Making it declarable here would let a check retire its
own debt by describing it, which is the collapse this vocabulary exists to refuse.
DerivationAbsence.title: DerivationAbsence

Direction.description: Which way a parameter has to move to improve a check's margin.
Direction.title: Direction

DomainKind.description: Whether a use sits inside the domain a check was compared in, or outside it.
DomainKind.title: DomainKind

DomainLabel.description:
Where a use sits relative to the validation domain. Never a verdict.

ASME V&V 10's distinction: a prediction inside the domain the model was compared in is
interpolative, one outside it is extrapolative. The label is the information — an
extrapolative check may well be right, and the reader is entitled to know that nothing
has ever been measured out there.

citation.default: ASME V&V 10 vocabulary (verification, validation, validation domain)
citation.title: Citation

DomainLabel.title: DomainLabel

LifeKind.description: What a life is counted in. Four kinds, because four is what the screens produce.
LifeKind.title: LifeKind

LifeQuantity.description:
A life a check computed, typed so a plan can read it without parsing prose.

``basis`` is the method that produced it — "ISO 281 basic rating life L10", "Archard
wear allowance" — and is required, because two lives in hours from different methods
are not the same number and a schedule that mixed them would say so nowhere.

``reliability`` is the fraction of a population the life applies to, where the method
states one: 0.90 for an L10 rating life. ``None`` where the method states none, which
is not the same as 1.0 and is never filled in here.
LifeQuantity.title: LifeQuantity

LimitSense.description: Which side of its limit a measured value has to be on to pass.
LimitSense.title: LimitSense

MarginUncertainty.description:
A sampled margin: the chance it falls short, its band, and what drives it.

``shortfall_probability`` is the fraction of samples whose response fell below
``required`` — the number a nominal pass can hide. ``lower`` and ``upper`` bound
the central ``coverage`` fraction of the sampled response. ``sensitivities``
ranks the inputs by their first-order share of the response variance, largest
first. Everything is reproducible from ``seed``.

citation.default: Monte Carlo propagation of input distributions; first-order (Taylor) variance sensitivity. Screening only — not a certified reliability analysis.
citation.title: Citation

MarginUncertainty.title: MarginUncertainty

Need.description:
One declaration a build required and did not receive.

``declaration`` is the field a document would state, written the way a document writes it
(``constraints.min_safety_factor``). ``dimension`` is the physical dimension it takes, or
``None`` for a declaration that is not a quantity — an element tag, a combination rule.
``units`` are spellings the unit layer accepts, so the report can say what to write.
Need.title: Need

PredictionSense.description:
Which direction of disagreement is the unsafe one.

The same 8% gap means opposite things on the two kinds of prediction a screen makes. A
predicted *capacity* measured low is the design holding less than the calculation
said; a predicted *response* — a stress, a deflection, a temperature — measured high is
the design working harder than the calculation said. Both are the unconservative case,
and which one applies is the check's to state, never this module's to guess.
PredictionSense.title: PredictionSense

Quantity.description:
A physical value: a magnitude and the unit it was expressed in.

Construct directly (``Quantity(magnitude=75, unit="kip")``) or parse from
text (``Quantity.parse("75 kip")``). The stored ``unit`` string is exactly
what the user wrote, canonicalized only to Pint's spelling of it.
Quantity.title: Quantity

RepairHint.description:
How to move a failing check back into bounds.

A failed check computes this deterministically — never an LLM guess. It names
the governing spec ``parameter`` by its stable name and the ``direction`` that
improves the margin. When a paired design inverse exists, ``corrective_value``
(in ``unit``) is the value of that parameter which satisfies the check at the
required margin — turning repair from a search into a single solve. Without an
inverse the value is ``None``: a direction is still honest, an invented number
is not. ``provenance`` records where the hint came from (the inverse function,
or a monotonicity declaration).
RepairHint.title: RepairHint

ScorecardEntry.description: One check's result: a name, a tri-state status, and a detail line.
ScorecardEntry.title: ScorecardEntry

Sensitivity.description: One input's share of the response variance, first-order (Taylor).
Sensitivity.title: Sensitivity

SymbolValue.description:
One symbol in a derivation: its name, what it means, and its value.

``symbol`` is the token as it appears in the symbolic formula (``"M"``,
``"σ_b"``), ``description`` the plain-language gloss a reviewer unfamiliar with
the source text needs, and ``value`` either a :class:`~anvilate.units.Quantity`
or a bare float for a genuinely dimensionless number (a friction coefficient, a
count). ``unit`` is a *preferred* display unit, used only when the document declares
no unit system; a document that declares one gets that system. Set ``unit_is_required``
where the preference is arithmetic rather than taste — see the field.
SymbolValue.title: SymbolValue

Underived.description:
A check's own statement that it has no formula to show, and why.

It rides on the :class:`~anvilate.scorecard.ScorecardEntry` in the place the
:class:`Derivation` would have taken, so it travels into the evidence bundle and
the JSON alongside the verdict it explains. That is the point of putting it here
rather than in a file addressed by citation: a clause cited by two checks — one
that computes and one that does not — cannot be answered once.
Underived.title: Underived

UnverifiedOrigin.description:
Where a third-party module's result came from, carried on every entry it contributes.

A module from outside this repository is loaded only when a user names it and runs
confined, and what it says is the module's word, not a check this library ships or
tests. So the entry names the module, its version, where it was loaded from and the
SHA-256 of the source that ran: enough for a reader to find and judge the code. An export
gate never counts such an entry as validated.
UnverifiedOrigin.title: UnverifiedOrigin

ValidationRange.description:
One parameter's range over which a check has been anchored or correlated.

``source`` is the worked example or the recorded test the range came from, so a reader
can see that a check "validated from 10 to 40 mm" was validated against two points and
not a continuum.
ValidationRange.title: ValidationRange

ValueSource.description: Where an acceptable value for a declaration may come from.
ValueSource.title: ValueSource

description: Anvilate scorecard: one typed result per validation check, with a rolled-up status. A check that could not run reports not_evaluated, which is not a pass. Generated from anvilate.scorecard.Scorecard.
title: Scorecard
